data.headline: Power Rankings Week 2: The Bhayshul Olympics Steals Gold By 0.66
data.deck: Adam leads the league in points for and still can't buy a win, while Taylor owns the only shart of the year.
body: Fourteen teams, two weeks, and already a graveyard forming at the bottom. Here's how the pecking order shakes out after Week 2.
Jackson is 2-0 at 272.64 points for and holds Manager of the Week, so he's the only guy here management doesn't wince at.
Trip is 2-0 at 268.16 after Amon-Ra St. Brown's 35.2 buried Aaron 105.36 to 73.52, a 31.84 point mauling.
Jeff is 2-0 too, riding Dak Prescott's 29.76 to a 118.56-105.98 win over Sean. Boring and great.
Adam leads the league in points for at 285.48 and got 42.5 from Jaxon Smith-Njigba, yet still lost 130.08-129.42. A war crime.
John crushed Josef 136.88-111.96, a 24.92 point beating, and sits at 279.78 points for. His 1-1 record is a lie.
Aaron scored 73.52 and lost by 31.84 to Trip. Frame that number, Aaron.
Bearcat rode 40.82 from Josh Allen and 39.5 from Davante Adams to a 23.1 point win, yet is only 1-1.
Josef put up 111.96 and still lost by 24.92. The Zyn can only do so much.
Ben lost 94.4-90, a 4.4 point margin that will haunt his bench decisions for a week.
Andrew is 0-2 despite 246.2 points for, the sad king of close losses.
Jack won 94.4-90 with the league's second lowest points for at 189.6. Surviving on fumes.
Matt himself edged Adam 130.08-129.42, the tightest margin of the week at 0.66, yet owns the third lowest points for at 205.38. Somehow he's still commissioner.
Sean got 35.3 from CeeDee Lamb and still dropped to 0-2 at 183.44 points for. His receiver plays better than his team.
Taylor is 0-2 with the league's lowest points for at 160.66 and the season's only shart. A clean sweep of misery.

data.headline: Fourteen Teams, Seven Wars, One Point Six Six Margins
data.deck: Somebody almost lost by less than a field goal and somebody else got embarrassed by 31.84 points in the same afternoon. Football is beautiful and cruel like that.
body: Let's rip through the carnage. Jack squeaked past Ben 94.4 to 90 in a game that proves ItsYaBoyJack can win ugly, which honestly might be the scariest version of him.

Bearcat put on a clinic, 120.72 to 97.62 over Taylor, riding Josh Allen's 40.82 and Davante Adams' 39.5 like he stole a cheat code. Taylor, meanwhile, picked up his first shart of the year for his trouble. Rough start, Taylor. Real rough.

Jeff's Chase Browns with Downs survived Sean's Burrowed Alive 118.56 to 105.98 even though CeeDee Lamb dropped 35.3 on him from the other sideline. Dak Prescott's 29.76 for Jeff was apparently just enough. Sean is 0-2 and starting to feel it.
Trip did not so much beat Aaron as evict him, 105.36 to 73.52, a 31.84 point beatdown fueled by Amon-Ra St. Brown's 35.2. Romo911 is now 1-1 and looking over its shoulder.
Nunnells edged Andrew 102.78 to 99.34 in the kind of tight one that used to be the closest game of the week until somebody had to go and ruin it.
John's BedBathNBIJAN22 stomped Josef 136.88 to 111.96, the single biggest scoring output of anybody in Week 2. Josef put up a totally respectable 111.96 and still got run over.

And then the main event. Matt outlasted Adam 130.08 to 129.42, a 0.66 point margin that will haunt Adam through however many playoff spots this league hands out, especially with Jaxon Smith-Njigba dropping 42.5 for him and it still not being enough. That is not a loss, that is a war crime committed by the schedule.
data.signOff: Fourteen teams, thirteen weeks left, and at least one grown man crying into a bowl of cereal right now. See you in Week 3.

data.headline: The Trade Desk Is Closed, Cowards
data.deck: Not a single manager pulled the trigger on anything this week. Zero trades. A ghost town.
body: Nothing to grade this week, gentlemen, because nobody in this league had the stones to actually make a trade. Fourteen teams, a bubble packed tighter than a Tayodin fantasy roster after an 0-2 start, and every single one of you just... sat there. Roster tab open, cursor hovering, then closed the laptop and watched football like a coward instead.

This is not a compliment to anyone's roster construction. This is 14 men staring at their bench, seeing something that should scare them, and doing absolutely nothing about it. Sean is 0-2 with 183.44 points for and apparently thinks the answer is patience. Taylor is 0-2 at the literal bottom of the league and didn't so much as float a package. Andrew got run over at 0-2 too and just... shrugged.
Meanwhile Matt won a game by 0.66 points and John dropped 136.88 like it's nothing, and neither of them felt the urge to consolidate or sell high either. Everybody just froze.

So the Trade Desk sits empty this week. No grades, no reasoning, no nothing, because you all decided inertia was a strategy. Somebody make a move before Week 3 or I'm assigning grades based on vibes alone.
data.signOff: Get off your ass and trade somebody. The SquirtRag will be watching.

data.headline: John Drops 136.88 and Still Can't Escape the Bubble
data.deck: BedBathNBIJAN22 put up the week's biggest number, but the standings didn't exactly throw him a parade.
body: Let's give it up for John. BedBathNBIJAN22 dropped 136.88 points on Josef and the Zyn-bo Squisher this week, the single largest output any team managed in Week 2, and by a real margin too. That's not a fluke score. That's a guy who set his lineup, hit his ceiling, and made Josef's 111.96 look like a JV scrimmage in comparison.

And look, 111.96 isn't nothing. That's the part that undercuts this whole thing. John didn't just beat a pushover, he beat a team that also put up triple digits, and it still took his best week of the season to get there by 24.92 points. Nobody's staging a parade for a guy who is 1-1.

Because that's the actual bad news here. John sits at seed 5, with a 59.6 percent chance to make the playoffs, filed neatly under Bubble with half the league. Nunnells and Trip are sitting at 2-0 without needing anything close to 136.88 to get there. So enjoy the top line, John. Frame the box score. Just know that in this league, one gaudy Tuesday-morning number gets you a headline and a seed 5, not a trophy and not a bye. The Bhayshul Olympics scored 130.08 in a game decided by 0.66 and got the same amount of playoff security you did. Math is undefeated. So is Trip.

data.headline: The Hardware: Week 2 Trophy Case Is Sticky Already
data.deck: Fourteen men, six trophies, zero dignity. Let's hand this shit out.
body: Pull up a folding chair and grab a lukewarm Miller Lite because it's award season in Squirtnite FFL, and Week 2 gave us a full mantle of nonsense to celebrate. No speeches, no gift bags, just numbers and shame. Let's get to it.
MANAGER OF THE WEEK goes to Jackson, aka nunnells, whose Ha Ha Ha, Now Heres A Guy squad put up 102.78 and moved to 2-0 like it was nothing personal. It was personal. It's always personal.

THE NAIL-BITER AWARD belongs to Matt, who somehow survived Adam's 129.42 outburst by the thinnest possible margin, 0.66, to keep The Bhayshul Olympics off the schneid. Adam, you lost by less than a point. Go stare at a wall.

THE MERCY RULE TROPHY is Trip's, and it isn't close, literally. 50 Shades of Zay buried Romo911 by a margin of 31.84 this week. Aaron, buddy, that's not a fantasy loss, that's a public execution with a scoreboard.
THE BIG DICK ENERGY AWARD for outright loudest number on the slate goes to John and BedBathNBIJAN22, who dropped 136.88 on Zyn-bo Squisher like he was settling a debt from a previous life.

THE SHART, already covered in gory detail up top, gets a courtesy nod here too. Taylor and Victorious Secrets sit at the bottom of the entire league with 160.66 points for on the season. Everybody clap, then look away.

Finally, the STUD OF THE WEEK trophy, no contest, goes to Jaxon Smith-Njigba, who torched the box score for 42.5 points and single handedly made Adam's Sunday both incredible and worthless at the same time. That's fantasy football, baby.

data.headline: Smith-Njigba Torches Everyone, Loses Anyway
data.deck: Adam got 42.5 points from one receiver and still went home a loser. Bearcat got two monsters from Josh Allen and Davante Adams and just kept his season alive. Football is fake and none of this is fair.
body: Let's start with the disaster. Jaxon Smith-Njigba dropped 42.5 points on the week for Adam, the single biggest individual number anybody put up, and Adam still lost, because that is how Squirtnite works and you should know that by now. First Down Syndrome fell to The Bhayshul Olympics by a margin of 0.66, so somewhere out there a bench player cost Adam a historic receiver performance and probably a beer he was going to buy himself in celebration.

Bearcat, meanwhile, is just out here collecting studs. Josh Allen put up 40.82 and Davante Adams put up 39.5, both in the same lineup, both feeding Hog tied and deep fried to a win over Victorious Secrets. That is two guys most leagues would build a whole roster around, and Bearcat had them both going off in the same afternoon.

CeeDee Lamb gave Sean 35.3 points in a loss to Jeff, which is its own small tragedy. Amon-Ra St. Brown put up 35.2 for Trip, who is undefeated and clearly not messing around. Dak Prescott chipped in 29.76 for Jeff, who now owns two of this week's top scorers and a 2-0 record to match.

data.headline: The Waiver Wire Sat There Like a Fart in Church
data.deck: Nobody added anybody. Zero trades, zero waiver moves, zero effort. Truly a banner week for the couch potatoes of Squirtnite.
body: I went looking for the Week 2 pickups to write about and found a graveyard. No adds. No drops. No trades. The trades list is empty, which means every single one of you fourteen dipshits looked at your roster after Week 1 and thought 'yeah, this is fine.'

And look, maybe you had reasons. Jackson at 2-0 with 272.64 points doesn't need to touch a damn thing. Trip is 2-0 too, riding Amon-Ra St. Brown's 35.2 and clearly feels untouchable. Jeff's 2-0 club got 29.76 out of Dak Prescott and figures why fix it.

But some of you had every reason to go shopping and just didn't. Taylor is 0-2 with 160.66 points, the lowest in the league, and still didn't lift a finger on the wire. Sean's 0-2 too, got torched for 35.3 from CeeDee Lamb on the other side of the ball, and apparently decided the answer was patience instead of action. Andrew sits at 0-2 as well and left his bench exactly as sad as it was last week.

Bearcat got 40.82 from Josh Allen and 39.5 from Davante Adams in the same lineup and still didn't need the wire, which is just showing off at this point. Matt won by 0.66 and probably should've made a move out of sheer nerves, but no.
Get off your asses next week. The wire isn't going to add itself.

data.headline: Three Unbeatens Cruise Into Week 3, One Matchup Smells Like Disaster
data.deck: The favorites keep favoring. Somewhere else, two rosters are about to fight for the honor of scoring the least.
body: Fourteen teams, 7 make the dance, 13 weeks left to figure out who's lying to themselves. Right now the truth is simple: Jackson, Trip, and Jeff are 2-0 and everyone else is catching up.

Jackson's Ha Ha Ha, Now Heres A Guy sits atop the power rankings and draws Matt's Bhayshul Olympics, a team currently tagged In Trouble at 30.9 percent to make the playoffs. That's not a matchup, that's a formality. Trip's 50 Shades of Zay, ranked second, gets Bearcat's Hog tied and deep fried squad, still finding its footing at 1-1. And Jeff's Chase Browns with Downs, unbeaten and ranked third, faces Andrew's winless Bibi's Ballers 69, who are 0-2 and need something, anything, to go right.

Now for the main event nobody wants tickets to. Ben's Jackson Off, treading water at 1-1, draws Taylor's Victorious Secrets, the league's certified basement dweller at 0-2 with the league's lowest points for total, 160.66. Taylor already owns a Shart this season. History suggests he is not done collecting them. Somebody is going to put up a number that makes the group chat wince, and all signs point to Victorious Secrets being on the wrong end of it again. Book the Shart Bowl now, thank us later.

data.headline: Matt Wins by 0.66 While Adam Sets Fire to His Own Bench
data.deck: First Down Syndrome drops 129.42 and a JSN masterpiece and still goes home 1-1 because The Bhayshul Olympics found six tenths of a point somewhere in a couch cushion
body: Adam did everything right this week. He started Jaxon Smith-Njigba, watched him go for 42.5, and probably started mentally drafting his championship parade route. Then Matt happened.

The Bhayshul Olympics put up 130.08, which sounds like a number a guy makes up to sound impressive at a bar, except it is real and it beat First Down Syndrome by a margin of 0.66. Point. Six. Six. That is not a loss, that is a paper cut that needs stitches.

Matt is now 1-1 and sitting at seed 10 with 205.38 points for, which is the kind of profile that screams 'we got here by accident and we are not sorry about it.' His playoff odds sit at 30.9 percent, tagged In Trouble, which feels insulting for a man who just won by less than a point but that is fantasy football, nobody cares how you got the win, only that you got it.

Adam meanwhile has the single best individual performance of the week sitting on his stat sheet, JSN's 42.5, and absolutely nothing to show for it besides a 1-1 record and 64.5 percent playoff odds. That is the cruelty of this league. You can have the best player on the board and still walk out with the same record as the guy who backed into a win with 130.08 and a prayer.

Next week Matt hosts Jackson, who is riding a 2-0 record into Week 3 like he owns the place. Adam gets a friendlier date against John and BedBathNBIJAN22. Somewhere Adam is still refreshing the box score wondering how 129.42 wasn't enough. It never is, buddy. Welcome to the margins.

data.headline: Aaron Gets Romo'd By His Own Roster
data.deck: 73.52 points. That's not a lineup, that's a plea for help written in fantasy points.
body: Let's talk about Romo911, because somebody has to, and apparently that somebody is me, sitting here at 2am doing math I promised myself I wouldn't do.

Aaron put up 73.52 points this week. Seventy-three point five two. Write it down, tattoo it somewhere private, because that number is now permanently attached to your name in this league's oral history, right next to whatever nonsense your draft picks were supposed to justify.

Trip's 50 Shades of Zay strolled in and dropped 105.36 on him, a 31.84 point beatdown that wasn't competitive at any point after kickoff. This wasn't a shootout. This was Aaron standing at midfield waving a white flag made out of his own bench, while Trip's Amon-Ra St. Brown quietly cooked for 35.2 and nobody on Romo911's side lifted a finger to stop it.

And look, I get it, everybody has a bad week. But 73.52 isn't a bad week, that's a cry for help. That's a lineup that looked like it was set by someone who forgot fantasy football was happening this week, remembered at 11:58 on Sunday, panicked, and just started clicking names. Meanwhile across the league Josh Allen was out there dropping 40.82 for somebody else's roster, Jaxon Smith-Njigba put up 42.5 for a team that still somehow lost, and CeeDee Lamb went for 35.3. Real players were having real weeks. Aaron's guys apparently took the week off to go find themselves.

Romo911 sits at 1-1 now, 227.44 points for on the season, tied for the number six power ranking, 62.3 percent to make the playoffs according to the math. That math is generous. That math hasn't watched this team play.

So congratulations, Aaron. You've officially given us our floor for the season. Every future disaster gets measured against this one. Every bad Tuesday waiver decision, every questionable start-sit, all of it gets held up next to 73.52 and found, mercifully, to not be quite as bad as this.

This is the part where I'd normally tell you to do better next week. I'm not going to bother. Just go grab every pitcher in the building, every keg tap, every leftover mixer from somebody's basement bar, drag them all into the middle of the room, and start working through them like it's a receiving line at your own funeral, because it basically is. Chug, bitch.
